reason: The validator targets 12 pure / table-driven functions of the rustre-decompiler crate (register_width_bytes, register_canonical, width_hint_from_instr, is_c_keyword, arch_from_str, parse_mem_operands, analyze_stack_frame, detect_heap_bases, render_c_signature, plus the binary-grounded load_binary/slice_at_va/disassemble_function_x86). The MCP server (wire_tools.rs) exposes only four high-level binary-and-VA-driven orchestrators for this crate: decompiler_core_batch_decompile, decompiler_recover_structs, decompiler_stack_frame_report, decompile_function_path. None of the pure helpers validated by the Python validator are reachable over JSON-RPC, so there is no common input space to compare on. This mirrors the rustre-decompiler-c gap.
gap_type: MCP surface gap — pure helpers not wired
recommendation: Expose the pure rustre-decompiler helpers (x86_register_width::*, pseudocode_generator::is_c_keyword, mem_operand::parse_mem_operands, callconv_bridge::arch_from_str, signature_recovery::{analyze_stack_frame,render_c_signature}, type_recovery_engine::detect_heap_bases, binary_entry::disassemble_function_x86) as standalone JSON-RPC tools in rustre-mcp-tools/wire_tools.rs so the validator can perform a behavioral diff. Out of scope for a single comparison turn; treat as a wiring task.
